business_problem: Credit Agricole needed a more modular and resilient information system so 39 regional banks could deliver secure omnichannel customer journeys, archive documents efficiently, and innovate faster than legacy systems allowed.
solution_summary: Credit Agricole Technologies & Services standardized its modernization program around MongoDB so shared platforms could support document-centric banking journeys across 39 regional banks. Squads and tribes build on a common MongoDB-based technical foundation created incrementally: the team identified requirements, validated a proof of concept quickly, then added supervision, monitoring, resilience, a rights model, documentation, and APIs before production rollout. MongoDB's document model lets the bank aggregate information from multiple systems into a single record for advisers and customers, which is critical for workflows such as mortgages and other digital journeys. The platform runs on internal infrastructure but can connect to the internet and scale when needed, while downstream analytical databases and data-science applications consume the resulting documents. This gives Credit Agricole a more agile, AI-ready foundation for branch, phone, and chat interactions.

solution_components.name: MongoDB
solution_components.role: Provides the document-oriented data foundation for Credit Agricole's shared banking platforms and digital journeys.

data_flow: Customer and adviser interactions from digital journeys such as mortgages are aggregated into MongoDB documents on shared internal platforms, then exposed through service APIs and forwarded to downstream analytical databases and data-science workloads for further analysis.
business_outcome: Credit Agricole improved delivery autonomy for product teams, created a scalable base for secure customer journeys, and positioned its banking stack for AI and generative-AI use cases.
